subject: docs/coop/artifacts/route-b.DR-007.preview-disposition.v2.json
reviewType: independent, refute not confirm; one of three subjects dispatched together
summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. Every attack axis fails. The distinctive risk on DR-007 is inventing a D9 code to make the preview tidy, and the artifact closes that off in four places rather than one: it refuses new codes in the authority claim, binds P-007-1 to 'a v1.14 code' with the forbidden cases enumerated, lists 'Any invented D9 code' among what must not be pretended settled, and refuses it again in whatThisDoesNotDo. The v1.14 pin matches live bytes and is the same digest the freeze binds D9 to, and the two verifier residuals it declines to close, R-V114-F1 and R-V114-F2, are real named residuals in the corpus rather than invented placeholders.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 53b72a910507e31dd8d20e29c8d3dd9c673a68944f086c7e33d9ca39af5f42b7, equal to the prompt's expected value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. I verified the prompt itself against the dispatch-supplied digest 50b49de6… before relying on the subject digests it carries.

The attack 'invents D9 codes or pretends v1.14 gaps are closed' fails on four independent surfaces. The authority claim says the artifact names what may be designed 'without inventing D9 codes or pretending the v1.14 gaps are closed'. liveContractNotThisDisposition states 'This entry invents no D9 code. Preview may emit a D9 exit using v1.14 without the observation→faultCause, optional-presence, success/policy/interrupted, or retention-loss closures.' P-007-1's bound requires 'The exit must be a v1.14 code. No new code for retention loss, observation→faultCause, optional presence, or interrupted branch.' And whatMustNotBePretendedSettled lists 'Any invented D9 code' alongside each unclosed branch.

The v1.14 pin is correct and corroborated from a second source. liveContractNotThisDisposition pins d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json at 8dd3303855f49bfdbb2751ee65f54a906405f0654159ebe815472f73cdf7da31, which matches live bytes and is the same digest IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE §3 binds D9 to — a fact I verified independently in an earlier cycle. So 'Live contract' is accurate, not merely asserted.

R-V114-F1 and R-V114-F2 are real. whatThisDoesNotDo states 'Does not close R-V114-F1 or R-V114-F2', and both identifiers appear in file 08, the claim matrix, IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE and the implementer blueprint, described there as verifier residuals tabled in §7 alongside 'the three checker-derived contract gaps'. That last phrase corroborates rowQuoted's decision text, which names three checker-derived gaps.

rowQuoted is faithful, tested by string equality against the live row: the decision text 'D9 JSON still has three checker-derived gaps and no accepted retention-loss result/exit integration' and the owner 'D9 authority + evidence/retention owner' both match file 08 exactly, and statusAtAuthoring HARD-BLOCKED matches its leading label.

The d070Note claim is true in the edited register. It states 'D-070 appended a preview-scope note to other rows. DR-007 still has no scoped owner-recorded disposition.' file 08's DR-007 cell contains no 'Preview-scope owner recording' note, and D-070's condition-1 snapshot row names DR-007 among the rows that 'remain without SATISFIED or scoped owner-recorded disposition'.

The attack 'hides D-002 rides' fails. D-002 attaches one ride to DR-007 — doctor's D9 mapping (DR-114) together with containment goldens (DR-G21) — and namedD002RidesIfOwnerRecorded carries both with the consequence 'Ships reduced, re-scoped, or waits' plus the T2-04 symmetry note that none survives on prose. whatMustNotBePretendedSettled repeats both as rides needing the successor.

whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA tracks file 08's needs cell closely: the register asks for a 'D9 successor for observation→faultCause, optional presence, success/policy/interrupted branch, plus reviewed retention degradation/refusal integration', and the artifact owes the same three items, adding 'without invented codes' to the integration item and independent review of the successor.

The attack 'coordinator becomes recording authority' fails: ownerWhoMustRecord names the file 08 owner and adds 'Coordinator may draft. D-000 does not make the coordinator the D9 authority.' condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded adds 'This file existing, or an ACCEPT verdict, is not owner recording', and whatThisDoesNotDo includes 'Does not owner-record this row.'

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED or condition-1 discharge' and 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' fail: status CANDIDATE-NOT-RECORDED, binds NOTHING, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, condition-1 effect scoped to 'architecture-preview scope only' with conditions 2-5 preserved and condition 5 named as the only authorization for docs/v2/implementation/, and whatThisDoesNotDo refuses both.

The selection authority is real and correctly characterised: D-071 is ADOPTED at commit 5f6b4e07bb9293041e494ab08d74942878a5af97, resolving to 'D-069/D-071/D-072: select Route B for DR-006/007/009', and whatThisDoesNotDo adds 'Does not re-adopt or overturn D-071.'

The remaining cited digests match live bytes: COORD 2af51835…, file 08 9495c70f… (the post-D-070 value), and the v1 predecessor at 40cceaff…. predecessorChange scopes the delta honestly: 'Retargets selection authority from CONTESTED D-052 to new-cycle D-071. Refreshes live pins after D-070. Adds T2-04 symmetry field. Does not invent codes.'

The honesty field concedes rather than obscures the limit: 'Preview condition 1 for this row, if later owner-recorded, closes by scoped disposition, not by a D9 successor. File 08 and D-002 both forbid inventing those codes.'

environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256 of the prompt and all three subjects at start and again at end with ls -l for permissions; digest verification of every cited input against live bytes; git log --format=%s at full hash for the selection commit; json parse of the artifact with string-equality comparison of rowQuoted decision and owner against the live file 08 row and of statusAtAuthoring against its leading label; corpus-wide grep for R-V114-F1 and R-V114-F2 to test whether the declined residuals are real; per-row scan for 'Preview-scope owner recording' cell notes; comparison of whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA against file 08's needs cell; structured checks of status, binds, sealRecommendation, the coordinator-not-authority clause and the whatThisDoesNotDo refusals; git status across the tree

acceptNote: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 advisories. The failure mode this row invites is a preview that quietly mints a D9 code for retention loss or a faultCause branch so the slice looks complete, and the artifact forecloses it four separate ways, including by binding what may be designed to 'a v1.14 code' with the forbidden cases named. Two claims I checked rather than accepted both hold: the v1.14 digest is the same one the freeze binds D9 to, and R-V114-F1 and R-V114-F2 are real residuals in the corpus rather than convenient placeholders to decline.
